kf: Keep the dressing on and **dry for 24–48 h**, then wash gently; **plain petroleum jelly**, no routine topical antibiotics.
Suture removal (typical): face 5–7 days, scalp and neck 7–10, trunk and arm 10–14, back, leg and joints 14 (up to 21).
Avoid strenuous exercise and stretching the wound for 1–2 weeks.
Infection: increasing pain, redness spreading **>1–2 cm**, pus, fever; **flucloxacillin** first line (check interactions for alternatives).
Scars mature over 12–18 months; massage, silicone and sun protection help.
myths: **"Antibiotic ointment helps healing"**: it causes contact allergy and resistance; petroleum jelly is as good.
patho_lead: Wounds heal in **overlapping phases** over months.

mech.t: Neutrophils and macrophages clean the wound (days 1–4); mild redness is normal.
Fibroblasts lay down collagen and new vessels; epithelium covers the wound (days 4–21).
Collagen reorganises and strengthens over 12–18 months.

comp: Infection, dehiscence, haematoma, hypertrophic scar or keloid.
